questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I choose Vancouver because of its easy access to nature and the fact that it is still a big city. Simon Fraser University takes good care of their exchange students, and due to its small size (compared to UBC and UofT) everyone knows each other which makes the exchange feel even better.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Had the best time of my live and met friends from all over the world. Hiked the entire fall with a lot of overnight hikes since the weather in Vancouver was super this fall, 20+ degrees until late October, and the we skiied in November and December.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy. The university has international student service which are very helpful and answers mails quick and you can also call them anytime.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received a lot of information from SFU beforehand and also had a zoom call that SFU facilitated. Also the website and Instagram has a lot of information as well.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I got my keys and found my room, very easy and a lot of staff there to help you. The first day is busy and can be overwhelming, but be open since it is easy to make friends.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
Towers (new and mandatory meal plan), Town Houses, MagTaggert, Shell House are all in Burnaby.

I lived in MagTag which was fine, not the best but I was never there anyway. If you choose between MagTag and Shell, choose MagTag!

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer:
You have to bring everything yourself (or buy).

Meal plans are optional for every housing except Towers. It is super nice since the Dinning Hall is brand new, however, it is very expensive... I think it is only worth it if you really hate to cook or you require a lot of food. Think a lot of the boys loved it! I just bougth a 25 pass and went there for dinner and lunch a couple of times. The rest of the time I ate with my friends in one of their townhouses, where we cooked and watched movies every night, super fun and chill. So I was glad I was not on the meal plan.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It does not matter too much where you live, you can also change after 3 weeks. Your friends will most likely lived all over the place, and because SFU is so small you meet people all the time and it is easy to meet up.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: All the exchange students who applied for housing right after they got the letter that they were accepted to SFU by their host institution got housing, so no worries.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very easy. If they tell you that you cannot take a course due to pre-requisites, then ask to email the professor and tell them about why you would like to attend the course. Also, if you end up waitlisted for a course you would like to take, go to the first class of the semester and ask the teacher after class if you can take the course, and then email International Student Services. That's how I got a course I was originally waitlisted for.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: First you list 10 courses, then you get verified to take them based on the courses you have taken at UCPH (pre-requsites), then you have to make your own schedule in terms of how many courses you are taking and overlaps, and then finally you have your final schedule.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: International Student Services are very helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all of the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try to only take classes on tuesday, wednesday and thursday - then you have a long weekend every weekend, and you can easily go on trip. Personally I only had classes on wednesday and thursday and it was the best! Also avoid Surrey and take some course downtown and explore the city.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Midterms, courses that are more debate courses than lectures, more assignments, classes with no computer allowed and only handwritten notes. Very different but you learn a lot and get to challenge your English.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I don't think the level was higher at all, but it was so different so I still learned a lot.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Much more like High School than Uni.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
CMNS 452 - E100 Race and the Media
CMNS 425 - Applied Communication for Social Issues
CMNS 443 - D100 Comparative Asian Media Systems

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Race and Media was one of the best courses I have ever had, super interesting and great teachers (Dr. Nawal) 
Also Professor Laba in 425 was also great!

Also check how your exams are, you can choose courses with only written exams and have a stress free exams period!

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Do not buy a Sim Card over here!! too expensive. It is easier to get a Danish card with international data (I got mine from CBB), soooo much cheaper.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food for sure..

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: SFU have a lot of sports team you can join and clubs - they have a fair in the beginning of the semester that you can go to and join as many clubs as you want!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Pools, soccer, dance, yoga, hikes, skiing - everything you can think about.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I played a little soccer which was fun - but for sure go hiking! British Columbia is beautiful and you need to take advantage of that. Everyone wants to hike, so it is easier to find other likeminded people to hike with!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to Joffery Lakes, Wedgemount lake, Whistler (both hikes and skiing), St. Marks Summit, Vancouver Island, Toronto - Canada has so much to offer.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer:
Very easy, it is not that far from Denmark - however they have a lot of homeless people which is very different from DK. However, they are mostly very nice and do no harm.

Also saying thank you whenever you leave a bus.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be open and even though it may be hard in the beginning, you will find friends! Push yourself to be social and say yes to everything.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: No not really, I love Canada after this exchange!

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The nature and the nice people

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Hiking Boots
Backpack for day/overnight hikes
Positive mindset and a winter jacket if you can fit it haha!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: SFU is great, and even though it is much smaller than UBC I have had the best real life college experience, where all of the exchange student know each other! E.g. my friend group with Danes, Austrialians, Sweedes, Norweigan and Dutch people met up with lots of others all the time fx to go ski in Whistler.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friendships and change of academic structure - and also the nature.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The first weeks meeting so many new people

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Enjoy! Vancouver is the best if you love nature and being outdoors and also SFU takes good care of their exchange students, so don't worry too much!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
